providers.name: Discord API
notes: Base URL https://discord.com/api/v10 (v10 and v9 are available; v6-v8 deprecated). Official docs moved to docs.discord.com/developers; discord.com/developers/docs redirects there.

Authentication: bots send 'Authorization: Bot <token>'; apps acting for a signed-in person send 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' from OAuth2, limited to the scopes the person granted (identify, email, guilds, guilds.members.read, ...). Some scopes are only available to approved partners.

Bot actions in a server are limited by the bot's permissions (bitwise flags serialized as strings, for example VIEW_CHANNEL 1<<10, SEND_MESSAGES 1<<11, MANAGE_MESSAGES 1<<13, READ_MESSAGE_HISTORY 1<<16, MANAGE_ROLES 1<<28) and the role hierarchy: a bot can only grant roles, and kick/ban members, below its own highest role.

Privileged intents (GUILD_MEMBERS, GUILD_PRESENCES, MESSAGE_CONTENT) must be enabled in the Developer Portal and, for apps under review, approved. They also gate HTTP: List Guild Members needs GUILD_MEMBERS; message content, embeds, attachments and components are empty without MESSAGE_CONTENT except for the app's own messages, DMs with the app, messages mentioning the app and context-menu targets. Since June 2026 apps must apply once they reach 10,000 users.
IDs are snowflakes returned as strings. Timestamps are ISO8601. Paging uses before/after snowflake cursors with a limit; read each endpoint's limits.
Rate limits are per route (headers X-RateLimit-*), plus a global 50 requests/second for bots; a 429 includes retry_after. Do not hard-code limits.

REST vs Gateway vs Interactions vs Webhooks: REST requests are made by the app; real-time events (new messages, member joins) arrive over the Gateway WebSocket; slash commands arrive as interactions (Gateway or Interactions Endpoint URL) and are answered with the interaction callback; incoming webhooks post messages to one channel using a URL token. This library models only REST requests.

Pinning moved to a separate PIN_MESSAGES permission (August 2025, MANAGE_MESSAGES no longer grants it in 2026) and the old GET /channels/{id}/pins endpoint is deprecated in favor of GET /channels/{id}/messages/pins.
From November 16, 2026, Get Guild Channels omits channels the bot cannot view.

endpoints.title: Get Current User
endpoints.description: Returns the user object of the requester's account: the bot itself when called with a bot token, or the signed-in person when called with an OAuth2 user token. With OAuth2, the identify scope returns the object without email; the email scope adds email. Does not return the user's servers.

authentication.header: Authorization: Bot <token>  or  Authorization: Bearer <user access token>
authentication.description: Bot token, or an OAuth2 Bearer token with the identify scope (email additionally requires the email scope).

pagination.details: Single object or complete list; no paging parameters.

rateLimits.description: Per-route buckets: the limit depends on the route (and sometimes the method) and is counted separately per top-level resource (channel, guild, webhook). Read X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset, X-RateLimit-Reset-After and X-RateLimit-Bucket on every response instead of hard-coding limits. Bots also share a global limit of 50 requests per second. A 429 response includes retry_after (seconds to wait), global (boolean) and message. IPs that make 10,000 invalid requests (401, 403 or 429) in 10 minutes are temporarily blocked.

scenarios.title: My Servers Dashboard
scenarios.goal: A student signs in to a study-planner website with 'Log in with Discord'. The site shows a list of every Discord server the student is in (server name, icon, and whether the student owns it). When the student taps a server, the site shows the student's own nickname in that server and the date they joined it.

constraints: The website has no bot installed in the student's servers. It only has the student's OAuth2 access token.
When the student logged in they granted exactly these scopes: identify, guilds, guilds.members.read.
The site does not know any server IDs in advance.
Load the server list with one request; only request per-server details for the server the student taps.

Needs a bot token in that server plus the GUILD_MEMBERS privileged intent, and returns every member instead of the student.
Get Guild returns server settings and roles, not the student's nickname or join date, and the OAuth2 scope list has no scope for it.

keyIdeas: Discord has two kinds of callers: a bot (Authorization: Bot) acting inside servers it was added to, and an app acting for a signed-in person (Authorization: Bearer) limited to the scopes that person granted.
The server list response is a JSON array at the root ([]), each element a partial guild with id, name, icon and owner.
The id of the tapped server becomes the {guild_id} path parameter of the second request.

flaws.explanation: Slash commands are interactions that Discord delivers to the app (here, to its Interactions Endpoint URL); they are not channel messages to poll, and there is no REST route to list interactions. Polling every 2 seconds also wastes rate-limit budget, and without MESSAGE_CONTENT the content of other users' messages comes back empty anyway.
Create Message posts an ordinary channel message; it does not answer the interaction, so the command is never acknowledged within the 3-second deadline.

Create Message flags can only be SUPPRESS_EMBEDS, SUPPRESS_NOTIFICATIONS, IS_VOICE_MESSAGE or IS_COMPONENTS_V2, so the reply would be visible to everyone. Only an interaction response can set EPHEMERAL (64).
Nothing records the reply's ID. The interaction callback returns it only when with_response=true (interaction.response_message_id).

acceptedPlans.label: Answer the interaction with an ephemeral message

steps.purpose: Reply to the received /hint interaction with a message only the invoking student sees, and get the reply ID back.

Without with_response=true the callback returns 204 No Content, so the reply ID for the log is missing.
Type 1 (PONG) only acknowledges Discord's endpoint ping; it sends no message.

Interactions must be answered within 3 seconds using the interaction's own id and token; the token stays valid for 15 minutes for follow-ups.
Ephemeral replies exist only for interaction responses (flag 64).
An optional parameter (with_response) changes 204 No Content into a JSON body with interaction.response_message_id.
Without MESSAGE_CONTENT, reading other users' message text returns empty strings, so a polling design would fail even before rate limits.
